$comment: How a served config line is named (F-307-g, F-307-h, F-307-j, ADR-0089).
The stored lines are served by two readers in two languages: billing's
config list (TypeScript, the panel's copy) and sub-service (Go, `/sub`).
A copied line and an imported `/sub` must show the same name, and nothing
can be imported across that boundary, so these cases plus a test on each
side replace the import that does not exist (the delta.json pattern). The
TypeScript half is billing-service/src/app/traffic/line-names.spec.ts; the
Go half is sub-service/internal/sub/line_names_test.go.
A line's base name: the buyer's `label`, else the tenant's `template`
(absent or `null` is `platformTemplate`) with `{brand}` as the tenant's
brand name and `{region}` as the panel's region, each replaced in one pass,
then trimmed (`templateCases`); an empty base keeps the panel's own name
and takes no part in numbering. The Grant is named as one list: configs
not retired whose lines are their current client's, oldest first (createdAt,
id), each config's lines in order, BEFORE a reader drops what it does not
serve, so both readers number alike. A name already given in the Grant
gets ` 2`, ` 3`, ... (the first not yet given).
Naming a line: `vmess://` + base64 JSON gets `ps` (re-encoded as base64 of
the JSON; key order is not part of the contract, so those cases compare
the decoded object, `expectVmess`); any other `scheme://` line gets its
`#fragment` replaced with encodeURIComponent(name); anything else is
answered unchanged.

lineCases.why: a line with no fragment gets one
lineCases.name: work

lineCases.why: the name is encodeURIComponent'd: Persian, space, emoji, reserved characters
lineCases.name: آلمان 2 🚀 a#b&c/d

lineCases.why: encodeURIComponent's unreserved set stays as it is
lineCases.name: A-z_0.9!~*'()

lineCases.why: a wireguard line is a URI like any other
lineCases.name: wg home

lineCases.why: a vmess line's name is `ps` inside its base64 JSON
lineCases.name: آلمان

lineCases.why: a vmess line that is not base64 JSON is named as a URI
lineCases.name: n

lineCases.why: a line that is not a URI is answered unchanged
lineCases.name: n

templateCases.why: no template is the platform's: the region
a template with no placeholder is its own text
one pass: a brand name holding a placeholder is not expanded again
an empty result is empty: the panel's own name

grantCases.why: no label: the platform template names every line; the second line of a config is numbered
two configs in one region are numbered across the Grant, not each from 1
a buyer's label wins over the template
a number already taken by a label is skipped
an empty region and no label keep the panel's own name (null) and take no number
a config with no lines takes no name
a tenant's template names every line without a label; a label still wins
a tenant's template that comes out empty keeps the panel's own name
